title: Two-week social calendar under platform and date rules
prompt:
Marlow Cycle Works is running Spring Tune-Up Week. Using only the campaign brief, write the two-week social calendar that leads up to it: twelve posts across X, LinkedIn and Instagram, following every rule in the brief.

Output the calendar first, one line per post, in date order, in exactly the brief's format:

POST <n>: <YYYY-MM-DD> | <X, LinkedIn or Instagram> | <post text>

Number the posts 1 to 12. Put each post's whole text on its own line, with no line break inside a post and nothing after the text. After the calendar, add a note of no more than 120 words on how the sequence builds from the first post to the last.

Character counts include spaces, hashtags and links. This is a draft for review; schedule nothing and fetch nothing external.

completion.check: All twelve numbered posts are present in the required one-line format; the first line bearing each number is the graded post.
Exactly four posts are on X, four on LinkedIn and four on Instagram.
All twelve posts are dated from 2026-03-02 to 2026-03-15 inclusive.
All twelve posts are at or under their platform's character limit (X 280, LinkedIn 600, Instagram 400).
With all twelve posts present, no platform has two posts on the same day and no LinkedIn post falls on a Saturday or Sunday.
All twelve posts carry #TuneUpWeek, and no post exceeds its platform's hashtag limit (X 2, LinkedIn 3, Instagram 5).
With all twelve posts present, at least one post dated 2026-03-09 carries the booking link, and at least one post dated 2026-03-10 to 2026-03-13 carries it again.

skill_adherence.check: With all twelve posts present, no post dated before 2026-03-09 contains a dollar amount, the price or regular price as a bare number (79 or 99), the saving written as '20 off' or '20 dollars', or the booking link.
With all twelve posts present, no post dated 2026-03-14 or 2026-03-15 contains the booking link.
With all twelve posts present, every post that states the $79 price also contains the exact sentence 'Parts extra.'
With all twelve posts present, no post uses the words guaranteed, cheapest or best, or '#1'.

With all twelve posts present, every dollar amount in the posts is $79, $99 or $20, the only amounts the brief gives. Where a post is written more than once, an amount counts only if every version carries it.
No post dated 14 or 15 March asks or tells the reader to book, or says places are still available. A calendar with no post on those two days passes.

Every statement in the posts about the shop, the tune-up, the price, the dates and the number of slots matches the brief. It fails on invented scarcity or demand (such as 'selling fast' or 'almost full'), testimonials, mechanic credentials, guarantees, extra services, or a price the brief does not give.

best_practices.check: No post is a copy of another post or a shortened version of another, on the same platform or a different one. Repeating the required elements (the dates, the price sentence, 'Parts extra.', the link, the hashtag) is not copying. It fails if two posts share the same sentences apart from those elements.
No post asks the reader to do two different things (for example to book and to follow the account, or to book and to share the post). A post with one ask, or none, passes.
